subject.title: refactor: move non-session runtime journals to SQLite

question: Should OpenClaw adopt agent database schema v11 while removing the public ACP streamLogPath and legacy memory-event path contracts in favor of new SQLite-backed inspection/export APIs?
rationale: Repository policy forbids autonomously advancing SQLite schema versions, and the permanent public replacement contract affects existing callers and upgrade behavior rather than being a mechanical implementation choice.

options.title: Approve with replacement APIs
options.body: Approve schema v11 only after the PR exposes supported ACP history and memory-event inspection/export paths and proves fresh and upgraded installations.

options.title: Preserve current contracts
options.body: Keep streamLogPath and the existing public resolver compatible while moving their backing storage to SQLite.

options.title: Split the migration
options.body: Land the audit and memory migrations separately while deferring ACP schema and public-contract changes to a narrower proposal.

recommendation.title: Approve with replacement APIs
recommendation.body: Approve schema v11 only after the PR exposes supported ACP history and memory-event inspection/export paths and proves fresh and upgraded installations.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged session/transcript SQLite foundation makes this contributor the strongest history-backed owner for the per-agent schema and migration boundary.
